title: feat: support collaborative issue quests
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Rewards each distinct linked GitHub author whose merged PR closes a `POLLEN-QUEST` issue
- Re-keys legacy issue rewards to the existing per-GitHub identity format so winners cannot be paid twice
- Hides assigned issues from the open quest board within the existing 60-second catalog cache
- Adds regression coverage for migration idempotency, multiple authors, assigned, and unassigned cases

Production read-only audit: 37 legacy rows, 0 missing GitHub identities, and 0 target-key collisions. The existing unique index aborts the migration if a collision appears before deployment.

Checks:
- `npx biome check --write src/services/quests/definitions.ts src/services/quests/groups/github-contributions.ts test/quests.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npx vitest run test/quests.test.ts` (32/32 passed)

gist.headline: Shared quests, shared pollen
gist.blurb: A quest can now reward every distinct GitHub contributor whose merged PR closes it. Polli checked the ledger twice, because duplicate honey is how spreadsheets become folklore.
gist.summary: Collaborative POLLEN-QUEST issues now reward each distinct linked GitHub author with a merged closing PR, while legacy issue rewards are migrated to per-GitHub-identity keys and assigned issues stay off the open quest board.
gist.impact: Contributors collaborating on the same quest can each claim the fixed reward once, with duplicate payouts prevented and already-assigned quests kept out of the available catalog.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy shared garden quest: Polli in a tiny foreperson cap helps several friendly developer bees place distinct named reward jars beside one flowering code-plant, showing that each collaborator receives their own Pollen reward. A small retro quest board in the background has one assigned card tucked away while open cards remain visible; use vines, flowers, and a glowing terminal to connect GitHub collaboration with the quest system.
